rows.evidence: Q1: Results section <U+2013> the authors apply their own design methodology to a sprinkler network in Albacete and a 127.7 ha citrus drip network in Valencia, running EPANET simulations, DIOPRAM pipe optimisation and pumping-plant energy calculations (Tables 3<U+2013>9, Figs 5<U+2013>6).
rows.notes: The study is a design-methodology paper with worked application examples (hydrant discharge sizing, maximum/minimum demand curves, pumping-plant energy estimation). It does not report any result of its own comparing the investment cost of on-demand networks with other delivery modes, nor does it quantify a cost penalty of guaranteeing peak-period supply. The statement that an on-demand system is expensive because of large conveyance capacity and flow control for peak demand appears only as an unreferenced assertion in the Introduction, not as a finding. Its own cost-related results concern (a) reduced installation cost by tailoring hydrant discharge to plot size with flow-limiting valves and (b) energy/investment trade-offs between variable- and constant-speed pumps (payback 5.3 years). All model runs are design calculations with no comparison against measurements from a real operating system, so they would not count as own evidence under the simulation rule either.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is methodological; its 'results' are illustrative applications of the proposed design procedures, not observations of network cost or performance.
